structure: The codebase has three strict abstraction layers: (1) PaymentGateway ABC — the provider contract; (2) StripeGateway / PayPalGateway — provider implementations that must never leak provider details upward; (3) PaymentService — the business facade used by callers. CheckoutController is the caller and must not know about gateways. A change that respects abstraction adds new capability at the facade or implementation level without changing the interface contract or leaking details across layers.

"""String utility module. Public API at top, helpers below, constants in a dedicated block."""

# ===== public constants block =====
MAX_SLUG_LENGTH = 64
DEFAULT_SEPARATOR = "-"


# ===== public API block =====
def slugify(text: str, separator: str = DEFAULT_SEPARATOR) -> str:
    """Turn arbitrary text into a URL-safe slug."""
    normalized = _normalize(text)
    words = normalized.split()
    slug = separator.join(words)[:MAX_SLUG_LENGTH]
    return slug.rstrip(separator)


def truncate(text: str, limit: int) -> str:
    """Truncate text to a limit, keeping whole words when possible."""
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    cut = text[:limit]
    if " " in cut:
        cut = cut.rsplit(" ", 1)[0]
    return cut + "..."


# ===== internal helpers block (module-private, not for external use) =====
def _normalize(text: str) -> str:
    """Lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace."""
    import re
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9\s]", "", text)
    return " ".join(text.split())
structure: The module has a deliberate block layout: constants block, public API block (slugify, truncate), then internal helpers block (_normalize, underscore-prefixed = private). The public API is the module's stable interface; helpers are implementation detail. A change that respects structure adds new public functions in the API block and new helpers in the helpers block, reusing existing helpers instead of duplicating or inlining their logic.

structure: The system is event-driven with three layers: Event (contract), EventBus (core infrastructure — the dispatch loop must stay generic), and concrete handlers (EmailNotifier, AuditLogger). New behavior is added by writing a new handler and subscribing it in wire(); the EventBus core and the Event contract are stable. A change that respects abstraction extends the handler layer without touching the dispatch loop or the event contract.
